Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the inferior and posterior wall of the left ventricle, which is the pathognomonic radiographic sign of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This location distinguishes it from mitral annular calcification (which would be more superior and central at the AV groove) or pericardial calcification (which typically follows the cardiac silhouette more broadly).
